a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, or poor vision, which requires correction with glasses.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, weak muscles, and is experiencing speech difficulties, where communication can be hard to understand.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and those typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences glue ear, where fluid builds up in the ear, and has complained of blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned blurry vision and has experienced glaucoma-like symptoms.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart, which is not life-threatening but requires ongoing monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, including an aversion to certain textures and tastes, making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences exhaustion easily, even with simple play, suggesting potential neurological or muscular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fluid buildup in her ear, which can affect her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and speech delays, which may be related to their overall health and development.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to have food cut into pieces or cooked until soft to make chewing easier.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding has been a challenge for many individuals with KBG syndrome, including cutting and cooking of food being necessary.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty concentrating and getting tired easily, which impacts her ability to focus in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education-wise, children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require support with behavioral or developmental challenges.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and exhaustion easily, affecting her overall physical and mental health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety are commonly reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies such as hip dysplasia and tethered cord can be present in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, eyesight (ophthalmology) review, and palatal review.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart conditions, treatment of fluid buildup, correction of tethered cord, management of scoliosis, and consideration of additional therapies based on specific symptoms and needs.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored, but so far it has not caused significant issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion to certain textures, making meal times tricky.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences more falls than her peers, indicating a need for increased safety during playtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatment.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated and covers her ears when exposed to loud noises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasal ventilation to assist with feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints a lot, which can lead to eye fatigue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to have her teeth checked regularly to prevent decay and ensure proper dental health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and tooth sensitivity are common in KBG syndrome, with some requiring braces or other orthodontic interventions.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developing at a slightly slower pace compared to her peers, but with the support of therapists and educators, she is making progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, but some may excel in specialized settings or traditional mainstream settings with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is experiencing developmental delays, particularly in reaching milestones such as sitting and walking, but with therapeutic intervention, these can be addressed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Overall, individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can be managed with medication and therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to complications such as scoliosis, and delayed closure of the soft spot on his head.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may also experience tethered cord, which can result in pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening:
   - Regular dental check-ups
   - Regular hearing reviews to age 5
   - Palatal review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns)
   
b) Recommendations for treatments:
   - Monitoring of septal defect
   - Management of seizures
   - Treatment of tethered cord (MRI)
   - Assessment and correction of hip dysplasia
   
c) Additional recommendations:
   - Work with therapists to help with developmental delays
   - Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fluid buildup in her ears, requiring periodic visits to specialists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and speech delays, with some experiencing subtler anomalies of the palate that may affect speech development and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when trying to focus on things, indicating potential visual issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires careful dental health monitoring and brushing to prevent tooth decay and chipping.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's cognitive abilities and developmental milestones may vary, but she attends mainstream primary school and has received EHCP.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require support with behavioral differences or speech delay.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires quickly during physical activity, suggesting potential neurological or muscular issues.

i) Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).
j) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
k) Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and behavioural therapy.
